reason: The text contains multiple instances of regular people exercising agency, particularly in the latter sections. Most notably, 'all the people from small to great' (כל־העם מקטן ועד־גדול) collectively rise up and take action to flee to Egypt in fear of the Chaldeans. Additionally, several military commanders and officers (Ishmael, Johanan, Seraiah, and Jaazaniah) who might be considered figures with some authority but not of the highest rank, demonstrate agency through their actions: coming to Gedaliah, swearing oaths, and later conspiring to assassinate him. These are portrayed as making autonomous decisions and taking independent action, not merely as passive subjects to royal decree. The narrative particularly emphasizes human choice and consequence in the post-destruction period.
